candidates.text: Firms consume not quotes but a fitted implied-volatility surface, from which prices, Greeks, and risk-neutral densities are derived (Fengler, 2009)<!--ref:S2--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->.

On a single date, call prices must be non-increasing and convex in strike, total variance must not decrease with maturity, and the zero-maturity limit must match intrinsic value (Gatheral & Jacquier, 2013<!--ref:S1--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->; Guo et al., 2016)<!--ref:P1--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->.
Across dates, no self-financing strategy in the option panel may produce a riskless profit (Niu, 2015 [preprint])<!--ref:C2--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->.
Construction is therefore constrained estimation rather than interpolation, run at scale on dense, noisy quotes (Wiedemann et al., 2025)<!--ref:N2--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->.

"Arbitrage-free" denotes at least four properties here: a parameter domain that excludes violations (Guo et al., 2016)<!--ref:P1--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->, a penalty that discourages them (Na et al., 2023 [preprint])<!--ref:N5--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->, a post-fit map that removes them (Bender & Thiel, 2020)<!--ref:R3--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->, or a generator screened before output (Bajalica et al., 2026)<!--ref:G5--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->.

These differ in how they fail, and the literature uses one phrase for the static condition and for the dynamic one, although the second concerns the joint law of a surface process (Niu, 2015)<!--ref:C2--><!--anchor:section:1.1-->.

One disclosed exception is retained: a single-stock panel (Stahl & Blauth, 2024)<!--ref:C5--><!--anchor:section:1.3-->, admitted because it tests a martingale-defect condition directly, is scope-flagged throughout, and is never generalised to index surfaces.

A surface is statically admissible if it satisfies five conditions: **SC1**, non-negative time value, $c(k,\tau)\ge\max(1-e^{k},0)$; **SC2**, monotone decreasing call prices in strike, $\partial c/\partial k\le 0$; **SC3**, the butterfly or Durrleman condition, $\partial^{2} c/\partial k^{2}-\partial c/\partial k\ge 0$; **SC4**, the zero-maturity limit $c(\cdot,0)=\max(1-e^{k},0)$; and **SC5**, calendar monotonicity of total variance, $w$ non-decreasing in $\tau$ (Anagha, 2026 [preprint]<!--ref:G6--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->; Gatheral & Jacquier, 2013<!--ref:S1--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->; Martini & Mingone, 2022)<!--ref:P2--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->.

The conditions are not interchangeable in strength: closed-form **sufficient** conditions on the raw stochastic-volatility-inspired (SVI) parameters guarantee SC1–SC4 on each slice, with a separate condition for SC5 (Gatheral & Jacquier, 2013)<!--ref:S1--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->; an **exact** characterisation exists for the SVI slice (Martini & Mingone, 2022)<!--ref:P2--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->; and the family generalises beyond SVI (Guo et al., 2016)<!--ref:P1--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->.

The canonical failure is instructive: the SABR (stochastic alpha, beta, rho) approximation admits negative implied densities at low strikes for long maturities, requiring a one-dimensional partial-differential-equation (PDE) density fix (Hagan et al., 2014)<!--ref:S3--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->; asymptotically, a family can be arbitrage-free in the wings while violating a condition at the quoted strikes (Fukasawa, 2022)<!--ref:C4--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->.

Repair and generation rows exercise the same conditions (Bajalica et al., 2026<!--ref:G5--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->; Xiong & Liu, 2026)<!--ref:R5--><!--anchor:section:2.1-->, which is why SC1–SC5 serve as the review's static predicate rather than as a description of one family.

A static condition constrains one surface; a dynamic condition constrains a family of surfaces indexed by calendar time, and its natural formulation is a filtered probability space on which the option-price process is a martingale under a measure consistent with the numéraire (Niu, 2015)<!--ref:C2--><!--anchor:section:2.2-->.
**D0**: no process-level condition is stated.
**D1**: a process-level condition is discussed, asserted, or diagnosed at model level, with no reported check of the constructed, date-indexed family.

**D2**: the property is inherited from the model class — a constrained state space, a static-admissibility-preserving stochastic differential equation, or a decoder that cannot emit a violation — with no check of the fitted family across dates.
**D3**: a process-level condition is stated **and** the constructed date-indexed family is reported to have been checked against it over a path or sequence.
The count rests on that rule, so both are stated: 0 rows are D3; three are D2 (G7, C3, G1); four are D1 (P8, C2, C5, R8); the remaining 34 are D0.
They are P8, R8, G1, G2, G3, G7, C2, C3, C5, and S5.

Four are central to the findings: a neural-SDE market model whose state space of statically arbitrage-free prices comes with an explicit disclaimer of a dynamic guarantee (Cohen et al., 2021)<!--ref:G7--><!--anchor:section:2.2-->; a path-dependent construction whose surfaces are statically free but whose dynamic consistency across the family is not tested (Andrès et al., 2026)<!--ref:C3--><!--anchor:section:2.2-->; a parametric family reporting time-indexed arbitrage probabilities, which is a statement about model parameters over time rather than a path-level test of the fitted surface (Barski & Wiśniewolski, 2026 [preprint])<!--ref:P8--><!--anchor:section:2.2-->; and a single-stock panel examining martingale defects, dynamic-adjacent but scope-flagged (Stahl & Blauth, 2024)<!--ref:C5--><!--anchor:section:2.2-->.

Boundary cases are flagged rather than forced into a family: two rows distort a reference function and also repair an existing quote set (Bender & Thiel, 2020<!--ref:R3--><!--anchor:section:2.3-->; Buehler et al., 2026 [preprint])<!--ref:R6--><!--anchor:section:2.3-->; one row's constraint is architectural rather than a penalty term (Cao et al., 2020)<!--ref:N1--><!--anchor:section:2.3-->; and two constructions are model-level rather than data-driven (Andrès et al., 2026<!--ref:C3--><!--anchor:section:2.3-->; Cohen et al., 2021)<!--ref:G7--><!--anchor:section:2.3-->.
(2025)<!--ref:N2--><!--anchor:section:3.1-->, and a foreign-exchange delta-condition paper by Fukasawa (2022)<!--ref:C4--><!--anchor:section:3.1-->.

Abstract coverage is uneven: 34 read in full, four partially (R2, G3, C4, S1), and three at title level (P4, P7, R4).
The corpus is 40 Level VI and one Level VII (Niu, 2015)<!--ref:C2--><!--anchor:section:3.2-->.

Within-study baselines are the only licensed comparisons — a hard-constrained generator against surface SVI (SSVI) and a soft-penalty network (Anagha, 2026)<!--ref:G6--><!--anchor:section:3.3-->, a generative adversarial network (GAN) against a variational autoencoder (Sidogi et al., 2022)<!--ref:N4--><!--anchor:section:3.3-->, a penalty model against an artificial neural network (Na et al., 2023)<!--ref:N5--><!--anchor:section:3.3-->, and a repair across five completion backends (Xiong & Liu, 2026)<!--ref:R5--><!--anchor:section:3.3--> — and they compare implementations, not families.

The recheck re-coded a 16-row sample, drawn as two rows per family with the family's boundary or weakest-coverage row included, plus every metadata-only row: P1, P4, P7, N2, N5, R2, R3, R4, R5, G6, G7, C3, C4, C5, S1, S2.
Family attribution is the review's coding: the blind recheck agreed on 12 of 16 and disputed only P/N/C boundary rows (P7, G6, G7, C3), flagged in Appendix C.

The purest case is arbitrage-freeness inherited from the structure of a generalised SVI parameter set, holding for all admitted parameters rather than only at the fitted optimum (Guo et al., 2016)<!--ref:P1--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->.

A second line replaces a sufficient parameter box with an exact butterfly characterisation, so the admissible set is not narrower than necessary (Martini & Mingone, 2022)<!--ref:P2--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->.

A third calibrates an extended SSVI parameterisation jointly across maturities, making calendar monotonicity a property of the joint fit (Mingone, 2022)<!--ref:P3--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->; its sequential slice-wise counterpart is available only at title level (Corbetta et al., 2019)<!--ref:P4--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->.

Three rows broaden the admissible shapes instead: a random-coefficient parameterisation admitting bimodal short-dated densities (Zaugg et al., 2025)<!--ref:P5--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->, a piecewise-cubic interpolation that guarantees its interpolant rather than its fit (Le Floc’h, 2025)<!--ref:P6--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->, and a bounded-factor model deriving static conditions while reporting time-indexed arbitrage probabilities, the only parametric row indexed by time (Barski & Wiśniewolski, 2026)<!--ref:P8--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->.
One row claims necessary-and-sufficient conditions for the SSVI/S3 curve but is metadata-only and cannot corroborate them (Klassen, 2016 [preprint])<!--ref:P7--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->.

The boundary with repair is real — a distortion of an arbitrage-free reference and a linear-programming construction both embed the constraint deterministically but certify a transformed object (Bender & Thiel, 2020<!--ref:R3--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->; Buehler et al., 2026)<!--ref:R6--><!--anchor:section:4.1-->.
A gated network whose slopes and weights make the price function frictionless and convex by design sits on the architectural boundary (Cao et al., 2020)<!--ref:N1--><!--anchor:section:4.2-->.
A graph neural operator trained on a ten-year intraday SPX panel reports adherence without a stated tolerance (Wiedemann et al., 2025)<!--ref:N2--><!--anchor:section:4.2-->.
A deep smoother adds soft penalties plus a plug-in correction for sparse quotes (Ackerer et al., 2019 [preprint])<!--ref:N3--><!--anchor:section:4.2-->.

A GAN trained with a static-arbitrage loss on the ALSI index states that the condition cannot be learned through the penalty route, the corpus's most explicit statement of what a penalty cannot deliver (Sidogi et al., 2022)<!--ref:N4--><!--anchor:section:4.2-->.
A second penalty model minimises violations and reports a residual rather than a certificate against an artificial neural network baseline (Na et al., 2023)<!--ref:N5--><!--anchor:section:4.2-->.

A derivative-constrained deep network embeds strike and maturity derivative terms in its loss and trains on SABR-generated data, so its adherence is an in-sample property of a simulated generator (Hoshisashi et al., 2023 [preprint])<!--ref:N6--><!--anchor:section:4.2-->.
The hybrid row is coded as a test because the review credits a proof only where a theorem over the admitted set is stated (Cao et al., 2020)<!--ref:N1--><!--anchor:section:4.2-->.

A linear-programming repair moves prices minimally inside the bid–ask with no cross-date claim (Cohen et al., 2020)<!--ref:R1--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->; an entropic projection to the arbitrage-free set proves the convergence of the projection, not the repaired family's admissibility over time (De March & Henry-Labordère, 2019 [preprint])<!--ref:R2--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->; a distortion of an arbitrage-free reference shares the observable with construction, with the Kahalé approach as a special case (Bender & Thiel, 2020)<!--ref:R3--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->; and a strictly arbitrage-free non-parametric construction calibrates by linear programming with positive discrete local volatility (Buehler et al., 2026)<!--ref:R6--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->.

An observation-anchored repair over 252 out-of-sample SPX days and five completion backends reports a butterfly violation floor of about 5.4%, so the repaired surface is not violation-free on real quotes, and a cubic-spline backend has the lowest reconstruction error after repair (Xiong & Liu, 2026)<!--ref:R5--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->.

A Chebyshev-tensor construction with a quadratic-programming stage reports under 1% static violations and 98–99% inside-spread coverage in calm years, with leakage under stress (Alvarez, 2025 [preprint])<!--ref:R7--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->.

A Markov-chain approximation over 2,695 SPY options and 28 maturities on a single date carries a maturity axis but no date-indexed family and no dynamic audit (Madan & Schoutens, 2019)<!--ref:R9--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->.

One row asserts transformations without proof or test (Zetocha, 2023 [preprint])<!--ref:R8--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->, and one extends the scope to joint American call-and-put smoothing at title level (Yao et al., 2026)<!--ref:R4--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->.
The family's baseline is the shape-constrained smoothing spline, which showed that ignoring the constraint matters (Fengler, 2009)<!--ref:S2--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->.

Two earlier constructions enforced nothing: a nonparametric inversion without an explicit constraint set (Bodurtha & Jermakyan, 1999)<!--ref:S4--><!--anchor:section:4.3--> and a semiparametric factor model on DAX data estimated without enforcement (Fengler et al., 2006)<!--ref:S5--><!--anchor:section:4.3-->.

A variational autoencoder over the parameters of stochastic-volatility models generates surfaces whose admissibility follows from the stochastic differential equation class rather than from the training objective (Ning et al., 2023)<!--ref:G1--><!--anchor:section:4.4-->.
A neural-SDE state space defines a family of statically arbitrage-free prices and explicitly disclaims a dynamic guarantee (Cohen et al., 2021)<!--ref:G7--><!--anchor:section:4.4-->.
A gated rational network is arbitrage-free by design (Yang et al., 2017)<!--ref:G8--><!--anchor:section:4.4-->.

Trainable hard constraints go further: the constraint is a differentiable but hard architectural element, and the row reports 0.00% violations at a $10^{-4}$ tolerance over 15 runs on synthetic SVI data (Anagha, 2026)<!--ref:G6--><!--anchor:section:4.4-->, while reporting higher total-variance root-mean-square error than an SSVI baseline and a soft-penalty network — the corpus's one paired measurement, and it runs against the claim that a stronger guarantee buys a better fit.
A VolGAN generates joint surface and underlying scenarios evaluated through hedging, with the enforcement mechanism undescribed (Vuletić & Cont, 2024)<!--ref:G2--><!--anchor:section:4.4-->.
A simulation approach places static constraints inside a generated process but is only partly available at abstract level (Cont & Vuletić, 2023)<!--ref:G3--><!--anchor:section:4.4-->.
A GAN denoiser reports lower mean-squared error and runtime without a guarantee claim (Ginart Belmonte & Cole, 2025)<!--ref:G4--><!--anchor:section:4.4-->.

A latent flow-matching generator reports that 90.8% of generated surfaces pass all tested static conditions, the corpus's clearest pass-rate statement (Bajalica et al., 2026)<!--ref:G5--><!--anchor:section:4.4-->.

The blind recheck agreed on this field in 10 of 16 cases (κ = 0.47), concentrating the disputes where an abstract describes a guarantee without stating a theorem, so the distribution is a coding result, not a reproducible classification.

Six rows audit their own output: a graph neural operator reporting adherence on ten years of intraday data (Wiedemann et al., 2025)<!--ref:N2--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->, a deep network with derivative constraints on simulated data (Hoshisashi et al., 2023)<!--ref:N6--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->, a repair reporting a 5.4% butterfly floor (Xiong & Liu, 2026)<!--ref:R5--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->, a Chebyshev construction reporting under 1% violations (Alvarez, 2025)<!--ref:R7--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->, a flow-matching generator reporting a 90.8% pass rate (Bajalica et al., 2026)<!--ref:G5--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->, and a hard-constrained generator reporting 0.00% at $10^{-4}$ over 15 runs (Anagha, 2026)<!--ref:G6--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->.

On the dynamic condition the rule of Section 2.2 gives 0 of 41 rows at D3 — 0 of the 36 in-window records and 0 of the 31 construction rows — with three at D2 (G7, C3, G1), four at D1 (P8, C2, C5, R8), and 34 at D0.

H2's fit-error clause is unsupported, since no penalty or repair row reports a lower fit error than a constrained parametric baseline on the same data and the one paired measurement points the other way; its burden-displacement clause holds, because weights, tolerances, repair steps, and acceptance thresholds are where the constraint work is absorbed (Na et al., 2023<!--ref:N5--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->; Sidogi et al., 2022<!--ref:N4--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->; Xiong & Liu, 2026)<!--ref:R5--><!--anchor:section:5.1-->.

candidates.text: A hard-constrained generator reports a structural guarantee, a 0.00% audit, and a higher total-variance error than two baselines (Anagha, 2026)<!--ref:G6--><!--anchor:section:5.3-->; a repair reports a 5.4% floor and selects a backend by reconstruction error (Xiong & Liu, 2026)<!--ref:R5--><!--anchor:section:5.3-->; a Chebyshev construction reports sub-1% violations with stressed-year leakage (Alvarez, 2025)<!--ref:R7--><!--anchor:section:5.3-->; a flow-matching generator reports a pass rate without a paired fit-cost comparison (Bajalica et al., 2026)<!--ref:G5--><!--anchor:section:5.3-->.
One row states a tolerance and a loss together (G6: 0.00% violations at $10^{-4}$ over 15 synthetic runs) but neither test power nor regime coverage beyond synthetic SVI slices.

One reports a rate over a real panel with a stated protocol but no tolerance (R5: a 5.4% butterfly floor over 252 out-of-sample SPX days, attributed by the source to rounding); one an under-1% rate with regime dependence noted but no tolerance (R7); one a pass rate over an unstated sample (G5); one adherence over ten years of intraday data without a tolerance (N2); one a residual on simulated data with no power analysis (N6).
No row estimates test power, and no row applies an independent detector — the corpus contains one (Neufeld & Sester, 2024)<!--ref:C1--><!--anchor:section:5.4-->, never applied to another row.
One row reports all three, on synthetic data (Anagha, 2026)<!--ref:G6--><!--anchor:section:6.1-->, showing the triple is reportable rather than idealised.

To our knowledge, based on searches of OpenAlex covering 2015-01-01 to 2026-11-23, as of 2026-11-23 no included study states and tests a process-level dynamic no-arbitrage condition for an equity-index implied-volatility surface; the nearest prior work reviews the conditions without testing them (Niu, 2015)<!--ref:C2--><!--anchor:section:6.2-->.

A generator that constrains maturity monotonicity has made a static claim (Anagha, 2026<!--ref:G6--><!--anchor:section:6.2-->; Bajalica et al., 2026)<!--ref:G5--><!--anchor:section:6.2-->, as has a repair that enforces it (Xiong & Liu, 2026)<!--ref:R5--><!--anchor:section:6.2-->.

The neural-SDE row explicitly disclaims dynamics (Cohen et al., 2021)<!--ref:G7--><!--anchor:section:6.2-->; the review that treats dynamic conditions at length does not test them (Niu, 2015)<!--ref:C2--><!--anchor:section:6.2-->; and the path-dependent and time-indexed constructions build objects along a time axis without a process-level test (Andrès et al., 2026<!--ref:C3--><!--anchor:section:6.2-->; Barski & Wiśniewolski, 2026)<!--ref:P8--><!--anchor:section:6.2-->.

Because the three model-class rows (G7, C3, G1) are coded inherited rather than enforcement under the rule of Section 2.2, the count does not rest on a reader's intuition about what "the model is arbitrage-free" implies.

The first is a **test-power and noise-floor study**, estimating the false-positive and false-negative rates of the violation tests the corpus reports and separating data noise from method error, with the 5.4% repair floor as its motivating case (Xiong & Liu, 2026)<!--ref:R5--><!--anchor:section:6.3-->.

Starting from a surface family with a stated process (Andrès et al., 2026<!--ref:C3--><!--anchor:section:6.3-->; Barski & Wiśniewolski, 2026)<!--ref:P8--><!--anchor:section:6.3-->, it would define a path-level condition and run it over a multi-year index panel, falsifying this review's bounded-absence claim if a tested condition existed under a different label.

The fourth is a **residual audit for proof constructions** — an independent detector (Neufeld & Sester, 2024)<!--ref:C1--><!--anchor:section:6.3--> applied to proof-bearing parametric and repair rows, reporting violations at a stated tolerance on observed quotes; it depends on the first, uses public panels, and falls to the review's own team.

What the corpus **establishes** is a map: four loci, four evidence types, a near-disjointness of proof and audit, and one paired measurement in which the stronger guarantee carried the higher fit error (Anagha, 2026)<!--ref:G6--><!--anchor:section:7.2-->.

The second, log index 89, derived no-arbitrage conditions for a delta-parameterised volatility surface estimated on foreign-exchange options and fell outside the equity-index asset scope; it was replaced by Fukasawa (2022), whose subject is the equity-index implied-volatility asymptotics.
**Audit** is the independent property defined in D.3: whether the row reports a violation, residual, or defect statistic on its own output.
**Time** is time-axis engagement as defined in D.4 (Y where the row's coded object is date-indexed).
**Dyn** is the dynamic-enforcement code of D.5: D0 none, D1 declares a process-level condition without checking it, D2 inherits a model-class property, D3 states and checks a dynamic condition.
**Level** is the evidence level of D.8: VI single study, VII expert commentary or narrative review.

A continuous-time *model* whose evaluated object is one date's surface (R9) is coded N: the model is dynamic in its class, but the coded object is not date-indexed.

Conversely, a panel used only as an evaluation sample is **not** engagement: R5 repairs one surface per trading day over 252 out-of-sample days, N2 fits across ten years of intraday quotes, and R7 reports year-by-year panels, but in each case the coded object remains a single date's surface and no claim is indexed by calendar time.
- **D0, none**: the abstract states no process-level admissibility condition.

- **D1, declared or described, not checked**: the abstract discusses, names, or asserts a process-level condition, or reports a model-level diagnostic of it, without stating that the constructed, date-indexed family was checked against it.

- **D2, inherited from a model class**: the admissibility property follows from the class the model belongs to (for example a constrained state space, an SDE whose coefficients keep the surface static-admissible, or a decoder that cannot emit a violation), and no check of the fitted family over dates is reported.
- **D3, stated and checked**: the abstract states a process-level condition **and** reports that the constructed date-indexed family was checked against it over a path or sequence.
It is coded D2 and reported as what it is: a property of the class, inherited by every member, unaccompanied by any reported check of the fitted family across dates.

The rule is deliberately conservative and it is the rule on which the "0 of 41" count rests: the count is 0 rows at D3, and the manuscript states that count together with the D1 and D2 rows by ID, so a reader who rejects the rule can recompute the count from the ledger without leaving the manuscript.
